clause_name: RLA-530 — Residential Lease — Subordination, Transfer, and Estoppel
library_question: Do the standard lawful subordination, ownership-transfer, attornment, and reasonable estoppel provisions apply?

blocks.text: This Lease is subordinate to existing and future mortgages, deeds of trust, and security interests only to the extent allowed by law. After written notice of an ownership or management change, Tenant shall recognize a lawful successor and continue Lease performance. Nothing in this section waives or reduces a bona fide tenant's rights under the Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act or another applicable foreclosure law.

Within ten (10) business days after Landlord's written request, Tenant must sign a reasonable estoppel certificate confirming the Lease status, Rent amount, deposit amount, known defaults, occupants, and other lease facts reasonably requested for sale, financing, refinancing, insurance, or legal compliance. Tenant may identify good-faith disputes in the certificate.
